```{python}
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

ROOT = Path(".").resolve()
if not (ROOT / "scripts").exists():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from scripts.b3_read_all_hh import read_hh

zip_files = sorted((ROOT / "data/raw").glob("*.zip"))
hh = pd.concat([read_hh(zf) for zf in zip_files], ignore_index=True)
hh["year"] = hh["time"].dt.year
hh["hour"] = hh["time"].dt.hour + hh["time"].dt.minute / 60.0
hh["date"] = hh["time"].dt.floor("D")

snap_files = sorted((ROOT / "data/snapshots").glob("*.csv"))
snap = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f) for f in snap_files], ignore_index=True)

my_sites = sorted(hh["site"].unique())
site_col = [c for c in snap.columns if "SITE" in c.upper() and "ID" in c.upper()][0]
meta = snap[snap[site_col].isin(my_sites)].drop_duplicates(subset=[site_col]).copy()
meta = meta.rename(columns={site_col: "site"}).sort_values("site").reset_index(drop=True)

def find_col(df, keywords):
    for kw in keywords:
        matches = [c for c in df.columns if kw.lower() in c.lower()]
        if matches:
            return matches[0]
    return None

col_name = find_col(meta, ["SITE_NAME", "NAME"])
col_country = find_col(meta, ["COUNTRY"])
col_igbp = find_col(meta, ["IGBP"])
col_lat = find_col(meta, ["LAT"])
col_lon = find_col(meta, ["LON"])
col_hub = find_col(meta, ["HUB", "NETWORK", "SOURCE"])
col_cit = find_col(meta, ["CITATION", "DOI", "REFERENCE"])

hub_map = {zf.name.split("_")[1]: zf.name.split("_")[0] for zf in zip_files}
yr_bounds = hh.groupby("site")["year"].agg(first_yr="min", last_yr="max").reset_index()
meta = meta.merge(yr_bounds, on="site", how="left")
```

## C1. Site overview

All half-hourly FLUXNET timestamps are in **local standard time** (no daylight-saving shifts), stored in a timezone-naive container.

```{python}
overview_rows = []
for _, r in meta.iterrows():
    overview_rows.append({
        "Site ID": r["site"],
        "Name": r[col_name] if col_name else "",
        "Country": r[col_country] if col_country else r["site"].split("-")[0],
        "IGBP class": r[col_igbp] if col_igbp else "",
        "Latitude (°)": round(float(r[col_lat]), 4) if col_lat else np.nan,
        "Longitude (°)": round(float(r[col_lon]), 4) if col_lon else np.nan,
        "First year": int(r["first_yr"]),
        "Last year": int(r["last_yr"]),
        "Hub": r[col_hub] if col_hub else hub_map.get(r["site"], ""),
        "Data citation": r[col_cit] if col_cit else "See Data and citation section"
    })
overview_df = pd.DataFrame(overview_rows)
overview_df.style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Geographic distribution of the five selected FLUXNET towers."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.5))
ax.set_xlim(-180, 180)
```

## C2. Data coverage

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Annual share of half-hourly intervals with directly measured NEE (NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0)."
cov = (
    hh.assign(measured=(hh["NEE_VUT_REF_QC"] == 0).astype(float))
    .groupby(["site", "year"])["measured"]
    .mean()
    .unstack("year")
    .reindex(my_sites)
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.4))
im = ax.imshow(cov.values, aspect="auto", cmap="YlGnBu", vmin=0, vmax=1)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(cov.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels(cov.index)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(cov.columns)))
ax.set_xticklabels(cov.columns, rotation=45, ha="right")

for i in range(cov.shape[0]):
    for j in range(cov.shape[1]):
        val = cov.iloc[i, j]
        if not np.isnan(val):
            ax.text(j, i, f"{val:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7.5,
                    color="white" if val > 0.6 else "black")

cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, pad=0.02)
cbar.set_label("Share of measured NEE (QC == 0)")
ax.set_title("Fraction of Measured Half-Hourly NEE by Site and Year")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

best_site_mean = cov.mean(axis=1).idxmax()
best_site_val = cov.mean(axis=1).max()
best_pair = cov.stack().idxmax()
best_pair_val = cov.stack().max()
```

**Coverage takeaway:** **`{python} best_site_mean`** achieves the highest overall average share of directly measured half-hourly NEE across its record (`{python} f"{best_site_val:.1%}"`), with the single highest annual coverage occurring at **`{python} best_pair[0]`** in **`{python} best_pair[1]`** (`{python} f"{best_pair_val:.1%}"`).

## C3. Summary statistics

For precipitation (`P_F`), the **Mean / Annual Sum** column reports the **mean annual precipitation sum (mm yr⁻¹)** rather than the half-hourly mean.

```{python}
var_specs = [
    ("TA_F", "TA_F (°C)"),
    ("SW_IN_F", "SW_IN_F (W m⁻²)"),
    ("VPD_F", "VPD_F (hPa)"),
    ("P_F", "P_F (mm; mean = mm yr⁻¹)"),
    ("NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE_VUT_REF (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)"),
    ("GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)"),
    ("RECO_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)"),
    ("H_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS (W m⁻²)"),
    ("LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS (W m⁻²)")
]

for site in my_sites:
    sub = hh[hh["site"] == site]
    rows = []
    for col, label in var_specs:
        if col not in sub.columns or sub[col].isna().all():
            rows.append({"Variable (unit)": label, "Mean / Annual Sum": np.nan, "Min": np.nan, "Max": np.nan, "% Missing": 100.0})
            continue
        pct_miss = sub[col].isna().mean() * 100.0
        mean_val = sub.groupby("year")["P_F"].sum().mean() if col == "P_F" else sub[col].mean()
        rows.append({
            "Variable (unit)": label,
            "Mean / Annual Sum": round(float(mean_val), 2),
            "Min": round(float(sub[col].min()), 2),
            "Max": round(float(sub[col].max()), 2),
            "% Missing": round(float(pct_miss), 2)
        })
    display(Markdown(f"### Site `{site}`"))
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=2, na_rep="—"))
```

## C4. Time series

Half-hourly carbon fluxes ($\mu\text{mol CO}_2\text{ m}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$) are aggregated to daily means and multiplied by $1.0378$ ($86\,400\text{ s d}^{-1} \times 12.011\text{ g C mol}^{-1} \times 10^{-6}$) to convert to $\text{g C m}^{-2}\text{ d}^{-1}$.

```{python}
daily = (
    hh.groupby(["site", "date"], as_index=False)[["NEE_VUT_REF", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF"]]
    .mean()
)
for col in ["NEE_VUT_REF", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF"]:
    daily[col + "_gC"] = daily[col] * 1.0378

check_zf = zip_files[0]
check_site = check_zf.name.split("_")[1]
with zipfile.ZipFile(check_zf) as z:
    dd_matches = [n for n in z.namelist() if "FLUXMET_DD" in n]
    if dd_matches:
        with z.open(dd_matches[0]) as f:
            dd_ref = pd.read_csv(f, na_values=[-9999], usecols=["TIMESTAMP", "NEE_VUT_REF"], dtype={"TIMESTAMP": str})
        dd_ref["date"] = pd.to_datetime(dd_ref["TIMESTAMP"], format="%Y%m%d")
        dd_ref["NEE_DD_gC"] = dd_ref["NEE_VUT_REF"] * 1.0378
        comp = daily[daily["site"] == check_site][["date", "NEE_VUT_REF_gC"]].merge(dd_ref[["date", "NEE_DD_gC"]], on="date")
        max_diff = (comp["NEE_VUT_REF_gC"] - comp["NEE_DD_gC"]).abs().max()
    else:
        max_diff = np.nan
```

**Aggregation check (`{python} check_site`):** Comparing our daily aggregated NEE against the official `FLUXMET_DD` daily product gives a maximum absolute difference of **`{python} f"{max_diff:.5f}"` $\text{g C m}^{-2}\text{ d}^{-1}$**.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Daily NEE, GPP, and RECO (g C m⁻² d⁻¹) over the full record for each site."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(my_sites), 1, figsize=(11, 2.7 * len(my_sites)), sharex=False)

for ax, site in zip(axes, my_sites):
    sub = daily[daily["site"] == site].sort_values("date")
    ax.plot(sub["date"], sub["GPP_NT_VUT_REF_gC"], color="#1b9e77", linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.85, label="GPP")
    ax.plot(sub["date"], sub["RECO_NT_VUT_REF_gC"], color="#d95f02", linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.85, label="RECO")
    ax.plot(sub["date"], sub["NEE_VUT_REF_gC"], color="#1f78b4", linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.9, label="NEE")
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.6, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
    ax.set_ylabel("g C m⁻² d⁻¹")
    ax.set_title(f"{site}", loc="left", fontweight="bold", fontsize=10)
    ax.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.5)

axes[0].legend(loc="upper right", ncol=3, frameon=True)
axes[-1].set_xlabel("Date")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## C5. Diurnal cycles

**Season definition (hemisphere-aware):** Meteorological seasons are assigned from calendar month and inverted for Southern Hemisphere towers ($\text{latitude} < 0$, i.e., `AU-Rob`):

* **Northern Hemisphere ($\text{lat} \ge 0$):** DJF = Winter, MAM = Spring, JJA = Summer, SON = Autumn.
* **Southern Hemisphere ($\text{lat} < 0$):** DJF = Summer, MAM = Autumn, JJA = Winter, SON = Spring.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Mean diurnal courses of NEE (top) and LE (bottom) by season across all five sites."
lat_map = dict(zip(overview_df["Site ID"], overview_df["Latitude (°)"].astype(float)))
nh_seasons = {12: "Winter", 1: "Winter", 2: "Winter", 3: "Spring", 4: "Spring", 5: "Spring",
              6: "Summer", 7: "Summer", 8: "Summer", 9: "Autumn", 10: "Autumn", 11: "Autumn"}
sh_seasons = {12: "Summer", 1: "Summer", 2: "Summer", 3: "Autumn", 4: "Autumn", 5: "Autumn",
              6: "Winter", 7: "Winter", 8: "Winter", 9: "Spring", 10: "Spring", 11: "Spring"}

month = hh["time"].dt.month
hh["season"] = np.where(hh["site"].map(lat_map) < 0, month.map(sh_seasons), month.map(nh_seasons))

season_order = ["Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter"]
diurnal = hh.groupby(["site", "season", "hour"], as_index=False)[["NEE_VUT_REF", "LE_F_MDS"]].mean()

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(13, 6.2), sharex=True, sharey="row")
colors = plt.cm.tab10.colors

for col_idx, season in enumerate(season_order):
    ax_nee, ax_le = axes[0, col_idx], axes[1, col_idx]
    for s_idx, site in enumerate(my_sites):
        sub = diurnal[(diurnal["site"] == site) & (diurnal["season"] == season)].sort_values("hour")
        ax_nee.plot(sub["hour"], sub["NEE_VUT_REF"], label=site, color=colors[s_idx], linewidth=1.5)
        ax_le.plot(sub["hour"], sub["LE_F_MDS"], label=site, color=colors[s_idx], linewidth=1.5)
    ax_nee.axhline(0, color="black", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.5)
    ax_nee.set_title(season, fontweight="bold")
    ax_nee.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.5)
    ax_le.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.5)
    ax_le.set_xticks([0, 6, 12, 18, 24])
    ax_le.set_xlabel("Hour of day (local standard time)")

axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)")
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("LE (W m⁻²)")
axes[0, -1].legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8, frameon=True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## C6. Your reading

### 1. Surface energy balance closure

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Turbulent heat fluxes (H + LE) vs. available energy (NETRAD − G) for measured half hours (QC == 0)."
for site in my_sites:
    sub = hh[hh["site"] == site]
    valid = sub[(sub["H_F_MDS_QC"] == 0) & (sub["LE_F_MDS_QC"] == 0)].dropna(subset=["NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS"])
    if len(valid) > 1000:
        eb_site = site
        eb_df = valid.copy()
        break

eb_df["avail_energy"] = eb_df["NETRAD"] - eb_df["G_F_MDS"]
eb_df["turb_flux"] = eb_df["H_F_MDS"] + eb_df["LE_F_MDS"]
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(eb_df["avail_energy"], eb_df["turb_flux"], 1)
r_val = eb_df["avail_energy"].corr(eb_df["turb_flux"])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5.5))
ax.scatter(eb_df["avail_energy"], eb_df["turb_flux"], s=3, alpha=0.15, color="#2b5c8f", rasterized=True)
lims = [min(eb_df["avail_energy"].min(), eb_df["turb_flux"].min()), max(eb_df["avail_energy"].max(), eb_df["turb_flux"].max())]
ax.plot(lims, lims, "k--", linewidth=1.2, label="1:1 line")
x_vals = np.array(lims)
ax.plot(x_vals, slope * x_vals + intercept, color="#d95f02", linewidth=1.8,
        label=f"Linear fit: y = {slope:.2f}x + {intercept:.1f} (R² = {r_val**2:.2f})")
ax.set_xlim(lims)
ax.set_ylim(lims)
ax.set_xlabel("Available energy: NETRAD − G (W m⁻²)")
ax.set_ylabel("Turbulent fluxes: H + LE (W m⁻²)")
ax.set_title(f"Energy Balance Closure at {eb_site} (n = {len(eb_df):,})")
ax.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=True)
ax.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.5)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### 2. Cross-site comparison

```{python}
annual_c = daily.assign(year=daily["date"].dt.year).groupby(["site", "year"])["NEE_VUT_REF_gC"].sum().groupby("site").mean()
seasonal_amp = daily.assign(month=daily["date"].dt.month).groupby(["site", "month"])["NEE_VUT_REF_gC"].mean().groupby("site").agg(lambda s: s.max() - s.min())
gap_share = (hh["NEE_VUT_REF_QC"] != 0).mean() * 100
```

Across the five towers, **`{python} annual_c.idxmin()`** takes up the most carbon per year on average (mean annual NEE of **`{python} f"{annual_c.min():.0f}"` $\text{g C m}^{-2}\text{ yr}^{-1}$**, where negative values represent net ecosystem carbon uptake), whereas semi-arid/grassland sites like `US-SRG` remain much closer to carbon neutrality (`{python} f"{annual_c.get('US-SRG', annual_c.max()):.0f}"` $\text{g C m}^{-2}\text{ yr}^{-1}$). **`{python} seasonal_amp.idxmax()`** exhibits the largest seasonal cycle in monthly mean NEE (`{python} f"{seasonal_amp.max():.2f}"` $\text{g C m}^{-2}\text{ d}^{-1}$ between peak summer uptake and winter respiration), driven by strong temperate seasonality in radiation and temperature. By contrast, the tropical rainforest tower **`AU-Rob`** sustains strong midday carbon uptake and latent heat flux year-round while showing inverted Southern Hemisphere seasonality (peak uptake in DJF/MAM rather than JJA). What surprised me most was the persistent surface energy balance closure deficit at `{python} eb_site` (linear fit slope of `{python} f"{slope:.2f}"` instead of $1.00$), reflecting unmeasured canopy heat storage and large-scale boundary-layer eddies typical of eddy covariance measurements. Finally, across the full multi-tower record, **`{python} f"{gap_share:.1f}%"`** of half-hourly NEE observations are gap-filled (`NEE_VUT_REF_QC != 0`), highlighting why filtering by quality control flags is critical when analyzing diurnal or energy-balance dynamics.
